clue.text: Wrongly taken to telling off

indicators.note: off here means wrong or not right, so the letters of 'to telling' are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something was taken amiss because of a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling off' reads as a scolding, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on TO and TELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Property obtained dishonestly or by improper means has been wrongly acquired.

clue.text: Provided when up and running?

parts.note: sounds like a system that has just started working, but it means meals or films served on a plane while airborne, and 'running' hints at fleeing

explanation.definitionFit: Services offered to passengers on an aircraft are those available during the journey in the air.

clue.text: Veranda not good for gnomes

indicators.note: not means the following item is to be left out of the word for veranda

parts.note: a loggia is an open-sided gallery or veranda

explanation.surface: A veranda that is no place to keep garden ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnomes' looks like garden figures, but here it means pithy sayings, an old sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes in the sense of maxims or aphorisms are collected sayings, especially those attributed to Jesus.

clue.text: Close encounters of a singular kind?

definitions.text: Close encounters of a singular kind?

parts.words: Close encounters of a singular kind?
parts.note: plays on the film title about alien contact; intimate meetings that happen only once, 'singular' meaning a single occasion

explanation.definitionFit: Brief sexual liaisons lasting one evening are intimate meetings that are never repeated.

clue.text: Record house as address going to the dogs

parts.note: a tally is a running record or count

explanation.surface: Logging a house as the address of someone whose life is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to the dogs' suggests ruin; it is literal, the hunter's call to the hounds. 'address' means a spoken call.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntsman's cry when the fox is sighted is shouted to urge the hounds on.

clue.text: On-air obituaries gripping city

indicators.note: gripping says the words hold the city within them, its letters running across the phrase

explanation.surface: Death notices read out on radio grip a whole city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Kenya is a large East African city.

clue.text: Retired: main basis on which the SE is left?

indicators.note: is left means these letters are left off the word for the ocean floor

parts.note: the main is the sea, and its basis or bottom is the seabed
taken as written, the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A question about where the south-east is abandoned, after someone withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed and is lying in it.

clue.text: Tree born idiot's hugging say

indicators.note: hugging means the letters for born and idiot wrap round the word for say

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person or idiot
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone born an idiot clings to a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: The white walnut of North America is a tree grown for nuts and timber.

clue.text: Expose girl's habit

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a habit is clothing, and a vest is a garment

explanation.surface: Revealing what a girl wears as her religious garb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a nun's robe or a routine; here it simply means a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of clothing or possessions is to lay them bare.

clue.text: Those ready for take-off?

parts.note: reads as aircraft or passengers about to fly, but a take-off is a mimicking performance, which these entertainers give

explanation.definitionFit: Performers who mimic famous people are always prepared to do an impersonation.

clue.text: Composition showing stuffiness: expected opening to be cut

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, airless atmosphere

indicators.note: the opening, or first letter, of the word for expected is to be removed

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A musical piece showing stuffiness, with its expected overture shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrapuntal piece built on a repeated subject is a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Limit vote to change theme

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the two words to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to restrict the ballot in order to shift the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical phrase attached to a character or idea is a recurring motif, in Wagner especially.

clue.text: Folly is briefly excused in madness

indicators.note: excused means let off, so that letter leaves the word for madness

parts.note: insanity is madness
is shortened to its contracted form 's leaves just S

explanation.surface: Foolishness is quickly pardoned as a kind of madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Senselessness or silliness is foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Map-makers around French city having to cease rowing?

indicators.note: around means the letters for the map-makers sit on either side of the city

parts.note: OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: Cartographers around a French city find they must stop their boating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a boat without its paddles has to stop being rowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat lacking its oars cannot be propelled with oars, so rowing must stop.

clue.text: Comic artist, Briton: he has no style

indicators.note: style here means a fashioning or arrangement, so the letters are put into a new form

explanation.surface: A British cartoonist who has no sense of style.
explanation.walkthrough: William Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist known for drawing absurdly elaborate machines.
explanation.definitionFit: This British illustrator drew humorous contraptions, so he was a cartoonist.

clue.text: Public houses?

definitions.meaning: groups of people watching or listening make up the public for a show
a house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A question about taverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectators at a performance form its public, and theatres call each such crowd a house.

clue.text: Hero's headless corpse is with community on board

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the word for corpse is dropped

parts.note: a body is a corpse
is shortened to 's gives S

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, written SS for steamship

parts.note: the board in 'on board' is a ship, SS being steamship
EU is the European Union, formerly the European Community

explanation.surface: A hero's decapitated body travels with the community aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero's' is the definition with 's standing for 'is', linking to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Ithaca in Homer's epic is a legendary Greek warrior.

clue.text: Set apart, as in suffering from 10, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the small word is placed inside the longer word

parts.note: a fugue (10 across) is a psychiatric state of dissociation, so its sufferer is detached from reality

explanation.surface: Kept separate, as one suffering a fugue might be.
explanation.walkthrough: A fugue state is a form of memory loss where the sufferer wanders from home, a dissociative disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut off or separated from something is to be detached from it.

clue.text: Pullman's reduced by a pound — given change: a tanner

indicators.note: given change says the remaining letters are shuffled into a new order
reduced by means one letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: Pullman railway carriages, made plural
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A railway carriage, costing a pound less, gives change of sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was old British slang for a sixpence coin, fitting the money talk; here it means something that tans you.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultraviolet lamp is used to give the skin a suntan.

clue.text: In which "art models" appear in paper

definitions.text: In which "art models" appear in paper

parts.words: In which "art models" appear in paper
parts.note: suggests life models in a newspaper, but describes the craft where models are folded from paper

explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding sheets into figures makes sculptures from a single sheet.

clue.text: Means to ditch suit

definitions.meaning: digging tools are the means to dig a trench
one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A way to get rid of a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' tempts as discard, but it means dig a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovels dig trenches, and the black suit marked with leaf-shaped pips appears in every card pack.

clue.text: Just before one sees the light?

definitions.text: Just before one sees the light?

parts.words: Just before one sees the light?
parts.note: suggests the moment before a conversion or revelation, but literally the time before daybreak

explanation.definitionFit: The hour before sunrise comes immediately before daylight appears.

clue.text: Forgetting to pray, starts spell

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out the word for pray from the longer word

parts.note: beginnings are starts
to beg is to pray or plead

explanation.surface: Someone forgetting to say prayers begins a magic incantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests magic; here it is a period, as a batting turn in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn or period of activity, like a batting turn in cricket, is a stint.

clue.text: Turn up in revolutionary situation

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the small word from bottom to top

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Arriving in the middle of a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitable position or role, as in finding one's place, is a fitting situation.

clue.text: Play on the truth?

parts.note: sounds like a pun on facts, but describes a dramatised presentation of real events

explanation.definitionFit: A film or broadcast drama reconstructing actual events is a play based on fact.

clue.text: Nice sweetener: it's for settling in Ecuador

definitions.meaning: in Nice, France, the French word for sugar
the former currency of Ecuador, used for settling bills

explanation.surface: A French sugar used to pay debts in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so the word is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for sugar and the former Ecuadorian money unit are spelt the same.

clue.text: It's hot in the frame

parts.note: it is sex appeal, written SA, and the 's is S
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something hot appears in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention; 'in' is a link word, though it looks like a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sliding window frame holding the glass panes is called by this name.

clue.text: Hero typically in the papers — that is by the way

indicators.note: in means these letters are put inside the word for the papers

parts.note: the press is the newspapers
ie, from Latin id est, means that is
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A heroic figure typically in the newspapers, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero was a priestess of Aphrodite in the Greek legend of Hero and Leander; 'Hero' is not a brave person here.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth she served the goddess Aphrodite at Sestos, a female temple servant.
